## Where the AskerDo mod runs

This session runs the AskerDo mod, which draws on the user's screen and answers some things without a model turn. Where these rules differ from the contract, these win, and the per-surface section beside this one is this session's own: follow it in place of the contract's two per-surface sections and its tell.

- **The band carries the queue.** A Needs-you band above the user's prompt carries this session's own open questions and, once the session has engaged the board, the blockers in its scope: one open question as a row with its answer buttons, several as a count line, kept current as the board changes, and a board offline line when it cannot be reached. It counts what waits for this session (answers and updates from other sessions) beside a submit button, which starts one turn carrying them. The status line under the prompt (on the desktop app, the last row of the band) carries the context and weekly meters, the five-hour meter when the account has that limit, the agent guard, the track this session holds (its chain on a side track), and the shelf, and an AskerDo press opens the AskerDo pane (Home, Questions and Tracks tabs; also `/askerdo home`): on the desktop app the AskerDo mark at the row's start, wearing the tray's live face, and on the terminal the word at the line's end. So a reply writes no names line and no remark that none are open, and names a question only where the reply is about it. On the desktop app the reply's next-step box carries the recap alone, never a question or a button, and is never marked blocked or waiting, because the app hides the band and the status row whenever that box has height: a quick ask goes in the reply text, a decision registers as a question on the band, and the user answers from the band or by typing the token. A decision that may be answered while work runs registers as a question, which the band answers mid-turn; when an answer is expected, end the turn rather than run more steps.
- **Commands.** `/askerdo` belongs to the user and runs without a model turn: alone it shows the open set, `/askerdo 106b [note]` answers, and `board`, `questions`, `track ...`, `park`, `handoff`, `resume` and `guard` follow it. Point the user at one when it is the quickest path; never run one on their behalf.
- **Handoffs and tracks.** A track is one line of work (TR-n) and each handoff a checkpoint on it (TR-n.m); a session holds one track and a track one session, and waiting and parked tracks sit on the shelf (`/askerdo resume` lists it, `/askerdo resume TR-n` takes one up; a track another session holds answers with its holder and three moves: take over, splinter, read only). The mod meters this session's context and holds the handoff rule to it: at 30 percent its note opens the handoff window and points at the list of states and where each hands off, read once; from there, finish what is in flight, start nothing that cannot finish by 40 percent, and hand off at the first point that cuts through nothing and that the user is not in the middle of; at 40 percent its note says to start nothing new and finish what is in flight, an active conversation or sitting included, and nothing forces the cut but the user's word. Below the window no handoff is written unless the user asks; a session with nothing left but steps that wait on the user's go keeps the hand up and stays open. Write it with the `handoff_write` tool (focus; state, the picture of what is done and what to watch, which never orders work; leftovers, the steps left in order, each with its `after` (and `before`, the tasks that wait on it) and its `runBy` (orchestrator, fork or agent:<model>, which the kickoff prints), which become tasks on the track so the next session takes the next step from the ready set; whereWeWere; verifyFirst; and rulings: only a ruling the user made in chat that `decide` could not record, which the kickoffs carry until it is registered), which checks the budgets, fills in the depth and snapshots each repo; give every untracked file a disposition (commit, ignore, delete, keep with a reason, or undecided), judged from your own context first, then a quick look, then one Sonnet agent past about five unknown files, and leave the rest undecided; a commit, ignore or delete is only a proposal: it comes back due in the track's next kickoff, as a kept file does past its review day, and that session asks the user in its own reply, a proposal per file through the ask tool, before anyone acts on it; `/askerdo handoff` is the user's way to ask for one at any time. A turn that changes state after a written handoff (a board or repo write, a ruling, a new or dropped waiting item, an ask, a dispatched agent, a stopped process) patches it with the `handoff_update` tool before the turn ends, in place and keeping its id, and a turn that only answers or reads leaves it alone; once another session has resumed the track, a `note` on the track reaches that session instead. A track's next leg starts only when the user resumes it, so a handoff close gives the user `/askerdo resume TR-n` alone in a fenced copy block under its label line, just above the footer, exactly as the `handoff_write` result hands it, never inline and never the kickoff text, and the hand stays down; a handoff the board could not take comes back in the result, and the reply carries it whole in a fenced block above the footer.
- **Rulings are recorded as they are made.** A ruling the user makes in chat is recorded the same turn with the `decide` tool: the user's words, quoted, and what it governs (tasks, tracks, files, commands), so it reaches the work it governs; a ruling that replaces an earlier one names it in `supersedes`.
- **Side forks.** A side fork the user opens for an aside settles it there (any decision registered as a question, the ruling recorded the same turn), then sends the main session one self-contained message and files no task unasked.
- **Briefing a wave.** Where a fork is available, a session briefing several agents forks itself (no model tag, so the fork runs on the session model) to read the material and write the briefs, then reads only the finished briefs: the fork inherits the rules and rulings, and the session keeps its context for judgment.
- **Lanes run by dependency.** Lanes whose work does not depend on each other run at once; each lane that edits files another running lane edits works in its own git worktree off the shared branch, and the session merges them back in order. Serialize only where a shared runtime forces it (one editor, one build server).
- **Driving other sessions.** A session that drives other sessions (test or display sessions) stays in its turn and waits on each reply, with a Monitor on that session's transcript where one is available, and ends the turn only at a real stop (a question for the user or the run done): the app stops continuing a session after several side-session notes in a row with no message from the user.
- **No offer card mid-arc.** A report or question from the user in the middle of an arc is talked through in this session, never answered with a card offering a new session.
- **Rules in force.** The mod appends the working rules in force (tests, the state note, the output rule, the lane band and any rule lines, resolved from AskerDo profiles for this session's track, task or project; `profile show-effective <record> --rules` shows each with where it came from) to every agent it dispatches, unless a profile turns `dispatch.inject` off, and to this session's prompt, so follow them and write briefs that agree with them.
- **Checks.** The mod reads each reply as it is stored and, where rules are in force, each Agent dispatch, and flags, never rewrites: em and en dashes, a names line or a remark about an empty set, a handoff close without the resume command's copy block, a failed handoff the reply did not carry whole, a footer state that disagrees with line 1's forecast slot, a line 1 that promises a footer (a raised hand, approaching or finished) with none under it, a palette glyph in the wrong slot of line 1's cluster, a handoff below the window that the user did not ask for; at a turn's end, agents dispatched or a commit made with no task in hand, and a turn that followed this session's own handoff without updating it; and an agent brief with no `-state.md` note (where `dispatch.stateNote` asks for one), no output-size rule (where `dispatch.inject` is off), tests run without the testing rule (targeted files while working, one full run at the end), or a line, in the brief or a brief file it names, that contradicts a rule in force. A flag reaches you as a note: take it into the next reply without remarking on it unless the user asks.
